title: ICE cotton continues to rise amid bullish factors
content:
ICE cotton futures hit fresh highs as weaker US crop conditions, Texas and Xinjiang heat and dryness, and rising crude oil supported prices.
China's State Reserve auction saw a 26th consecutive sell-out, taking cumulative sales to 208,545 tonnes.
Open interest rose for a 16th session; further gains depend on textile mills accepting higher cotton prices and building orders.

title: India urges Bangladesh to lift ban on yarn imports through land ports
content:
India has urged Bangladesh to lift restrictions on yarn imports through land ports. The request was made by Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi to Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir. 
Trivedi discussed reopening closed border haats and fully operationalising land ports. 
India can back Bangladesh’s RMG sector by supplying zippers, machinery and other inputs, Trivedi said.

title: MMCF cost divergence could reshape Q4 fibre sourcing
content:
Modal 1.4 denier fibre prices stayed largely stable in Asia in the week ending August 21, 2026; China held at CNY 23,302 per tonne and Pakistan rose 0.27 per cent to PKR 756 per kilogram.
India diverged as Domestic Modal 30/1 yarn rose 1.11 per cent to ₹273 and 40/1 rose 1.01 per cent to ₹299, while Tencel yarn jumped over 6 per cent amid tighter lyocell supply.

title: Bangladesh eyes global capital with $2-bn Hong Kong fund
content:
Bangladesh plans a $2 billion equity fund in Hong Kong to widen business financing beyond conventional bank loans. 
Export sectors including ready-made garments, textiles, home textiles, leather and footwear could gain a capital route for upgrades. 
The government is also weighing dollar, panda and samurai bonds while pursuing customs, tax and capital-market reforms.

title: Invest Bangladesh begins operations as unified investor platform
content:
Bangladesh has launched Invest Bangladesh, merging its investment, economic-zone and public-private partnership agencies under the Prime Minister's Office. 
For textile, apparel and sourcing investors, it centralises facilitation, zones, approvals, incentives and other government services. 
It will retain BanglaBiz, work on 14-day business licensing and issue a progress report within 180 days.

title: Cambodia report urges action on energy supply shocks
content:
Cambodia’s reliance on imported fuel and fertiliser leaves its economy exposed to global energy disruption, a CDRI report says.
Policy options include energy diversification, green skills and strategic reserves for fuel and fertiliser.
ADB’s $250 million RISE loan will support poor households, tuktuk drivers and rural households.

title: Vietnam targets stronger ASEAN role through digital trade integration
content:
Vietnam is being urged to shift from low-cost production into higher-value regional supply-chain roles through clusters, infrastructure and transparency.
ASEAN’s DEFA, due for completion in 2026, targets digital trade barriers across e-commerce, payments, invoicing, data and cybersecurity.
Exporters and manufacturers face readiness gaps but could gain scale, resilience and better market.

title: India, GCC review FTA talks ahead of September ministerial meeting
content:
India and the GCC reviewed progress on proposed FTA negotiations during talks in Riyadh between Indian ambassador Vipul and GCC secretary general Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi. 
Discussions also covered bilateral cooperation, high-level engagements, regional developments and preparations for a ministerial meeting next month. 
Both sides stressed continued coordination on shared interests.

title: Sweden’s apparel imports fall as China strengthens market share
content:
Sweden’s apparel imports fell 2.6 per cent year on year to $2.422 billion in H1 2026, but Asian suppliers strengthened their position.
China’s shipments rose 5.8 per cent to $447.859 million, lifting its share to 18.48 per cent, while Bangladesh retained second place.
Denmark, Germany and Poland posted double-digit declines; cotton and trousers and shorts led fibre and product categories.

title: Australia's City Chic's FY26 EBITDA surges 92% on margin
content:
City Chic Collective's FY26 underlying EBITDA rose 92 per cent to A$12.3 million, while trading margin reached 60.6 per cent.
ANZ revenue grew 7.6 per cent, but US sales fell as tariff uncertainty prompted lower purchasing and pressured partner sales.
FY27 starts with stronger ANZ stores and improving US momentum, backed by lower costs, leaner inventory and undrawn debt capacity.

title: Can Bangladesh’s $38.7 bn RMG sector withstand 100+ mill shutdown
content:
More than 100 textile factories in Narsingdi have stopped or severely curtailed production, while BTMA says over 900 member mills nationwide are shut.
TexPro data shows China supplied 89.5 per cent of Bangladesh’s selected knitted-fabric imports in January–May 2026.
RMG exports reached $38.70 billion in FY2025-26, but August outages may test lead times and local value addition.
